svg.title: Organization GitOps delivery flow with Argo CD
svg.desc: A secure delivery flow from pull request checks through immutable image promotion and Argo CD reconciliation to Kubernetes, ingress, DNS, monitoring, and rollback. Red notes identify bootstrap gaps in the current repository.
svg.text: GitOps delivery: code to a running website
Target operating model for this repository • verified code path and outstanding cluster bootstrap are shown separately
GREEN = configured automation in GitHub Actions
AMBER = operator setup / not yet automated
AMBER = controlled prerequisite before live rollout
1. Change and quality gates
Developer change
Code, Dockerfile, Helm chart, Terraform
Small change set • peer review • CODEOWNERS
No secrets or environment-specific credentials in Git
Pull request checks
Node syntax • container build • Terraform validation
Review and required checks before merge to main
PRs do not publish images or apply infrastructure
Merge to main • trusted release source
Protected branch • least-privilege GitHub Environment • OIDC for cloud identity
Terraform validation is separate from Terraform apply; apply remains an infrastructure change
2. Build once, promote by immutable digest/tag
GitHub Actions builds and publishes to GHCR
Image tag = source commit SHA • anonymous pull check • no deployment from PR code
The repository also publishes :latest for convenience; production desired state uses the SHA tag
Promote the exact image into Git desired state
Workflow updates helm/my-app/values.yaml with the 40-character image SHA
Current implementation pushes a bot commit to main; branch protection must explicitly permit it.
For stricter review, use an approved promotion PR instead of granting a main-branch bypass.
3. Argo CD pulls desired state and reconciles the cluster
One-time platform bootstrap
Provision cluster • validate capacity
Install Argo CD • secure access / SSO
Not installed by the current Terraform templates
Keep the admin endpoint private
Argo CD control plane
Watches the Git repository / main
Scoped AppProject • automated sync
Prune removed resources • self-heal drift
Controller availability and RBAC are operational concerns
Helm desired state
Chart: helm/my-app
Namespace: production
Image SHA • replicas • probes • resources
Git is the source of truth; no CI kubectl set image
CONTROLLED PREREQUISITES: bootstrap, ownership, and edge configuration
AWS / GCP / Azure cloud-init still applies the app directly (usually namespace default).
Argo CD targets production. These two paths can drift or create duplicate workloads.
Ingress/TLS/DNS also differ: chart asks for nginx; GCP bootstrap configures Traefik; Helm has no TLS rule.
4. Runtime, traffic, and operations
Kubernetes workload
Deployment • readiness/liveness
Service • resource requests/limits
Rollout health gates availability
Ingress / cloud edge
Controller + external address
TLS/cert integration (not yet configured)
Provider-specific DNS / load balancer
DNS and browser
DNS points hostname to edge
User receives HTTPS website
Verify health endpoint after release
Observe / alert
Prometheus scrapes /metrics
Grafana dashboards + alerts
SLOs, logs, incident response
Safe rollback
Revert the Helm image-SHA change in Git (or promote a known-good SHA).
Argo CD detects the commit and reconciles the previous version.
Keep image tags immutable; avoid emergency live edits that create drift.
Organization guardrails
PR approvals • OIDC • least privilege • protected environments
Image provenance / scanning • backups • audit trail
Capacity, HA, DNS/TLS ownership, cost budgets, and on-call runbooks
Read this as a design plus an honest implementation status
GitHub image build and SHA promotion are automated; Argo definitions are in Git.
Controller install, ownership migration, capacity/edge review, and live DNS/health verification are the final operator checklist.
No cloud infrastructure was provisioned and no production website health check was performed for this diagram.
